floating_point: USED: the closed forms come from exact Fraction series arithmetic (pseries.py, exact.py). The published enclosures, however, are computed by ia.py, elem.py and gam.py in IEEE binary64, with one-ulp outward widening via math.nextafter after each basic operation and hand-derived a priori bounds for the exp/log/atan series. Some remainder terms are evaluated in undirected binary64, for example the elem._atanh_series tail with a safety factor 2, and the publication margin MARGIN*abs(iv) in certificate.pub. certificate.py also compares the d=1 reductions in plain floats (d1_float). This is float-based interval reasoning whose soundness rests on unreviewed rounding analyses.

USED: the certificate runs in binary64. ia.py rounds +, -, *, / and sqrt to nearest and then widens outward by one ulp with math.nextafter (lines 1-6, 14-57). exp(-y) is a reduced Taylor polynomial with an a priori floating error bound (56u + 1e-19) e^0.75 (NOTE.md lines 318-319). Root brackets rest on an a priori binary64 rounding-error bound in _sgn_f (boxes.py lines 81-94). libm pow, acos and cos supply only seeds (lines 97-136). Published intervals are widened by 1e-7 relative (certificate.py line 40). The IEEE-basic-operation widening is directed; the a priori error bounds are hand analysis.

USED: the enclosures are computed by ia.py, elem.py, consts.py, cx.py and d3.py in IEEE binary64, with one-ulp outward widening (math.nextafter) per basic operation and hand-derived a priori bounds for the series (NOTE.md 254-270). gauss.py locates Gauss-Legendre nodes in exact rationals from float Newton seeds, but the weights, function bounds and sums are binary64 intervals. NOTE.md 365-374 records out-of-trajectory limits of this library: d3._sub can lose 2^-57, and ia.mul((0,0),(inf,inf)) returns NaN.
